verses.text: But the Israelites were unfaithful about the things set apart for destruction. Achan, son of Carmi, son of Zabdi, son of Zerah, from the tribe of Judah, took some of them. So the LORD was very angry with Israel.
Joshua sent men from Jericho to Ai, near Beth Aven, east of Bethel. He told them, "Go up and spy out the land." So the men went up and spied out Ai.
They came back to Joshua and said, "Not all the people need to go. Send about two or three thousand men to attack Ai. Do not tire out the whole army, because there are only a few people there."
So about three thousand men went up, but they ran away from the men of Ai.

The men of Ai killed about thirty-six of them. They chased the Israelites from the city gate as far as Shebarim and struck them down on the slope. The people's hearts melted with fear and became like water.
Joshua tore his clothes and lay face down on the ground in front of the LORD's box until evening. The leaders of Israel did the same and threw dust on their heads.

Joshua said, "Oh, Lord GOD, why did you bring these people across the Jordan at all? Just to hand us over to the Amorites to destroy us? If only we had been happy to stay on the other side of the Jordan!
Lord, what can I say, now that Israel has turned and run from its enemies?
The Canaanites and everyone else in the land will hear about it. They will surround us and wipe our name off the earth. Then what will you do for your own great name?"
The LORD said to Joshua, "Get up! Why are you lying on your face?

Israel has sinned. They have broken my covenant that I commanded them to keep. They have taken some of the things set apart for destruction. They have stolen, they have lied, and they have hidden the things with their own belongings.

That is why the Israelites cannot stand against their enemies. They turn and run, because they themselves are now set apart for destruction. I will not be with you any more unless you destroy what is set apart among you.

Get up! Make the people holy. Tell them, 'Make yourselves holy for tomorrow, because the LORD, the God of Israel, says: There are things set apart for destruction among you, Israel. You cannot stand against your enemies until you remove them.

In the morning, come forward tribe by tribe. The tribe the LORD chooses will come forward clan by clan. The clan the LORD chooses will come forward family by family. The family the LORD chooses will come forward man by man.
The one caught with the forbidden things will be burned with fire, along with all he has, because he broke the LORD's covenant and did a shameful thing in Israel.'"
Early the next morning Joshua had Israel come forward tribe by tribe, and the tribe of Judah was chosen.
The clans of Judah came forward, and the clan of Zerah was chosen. The clan of Zerah came forward man by man, and Zabdi's family was chosen.
Zabdi's family came forward man by man, and Achan, son of Carmi, son of Zabdi, son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, was chosen.
Joshua said to Achan, "My son, give glory to the LORD, the God of Israel, and confess to him. Tell me what you have done. Do not hide it from me."
Achan answered Joshua, "It is true. I have sinned against the LORD, the God of Israel. This is what I did.

Among the things we took, I saw a beautiful robe from Babylon, about two kilograms of silver, and a bar of gold weighing more than half a kilogram. I wanted them, so I took them. They are buried in the ground inside my tent, with the silver underneath."
So Joshua sent messengers, and they ran to the tent. There it was, hidden in his tent, with the silver underneath.
They took the things out of the tent, brought them to Joshua and all the Israelites, and spread them out before the LORD.

Then Joshua, together with all Israel, took Achan son of Zerah, the silver, the robe, the gold bar, his sons and daughters, his cattle, donkeys and sheep, his tent and everything he had, to the Valley of Achor.
Joshua said, "Why have you brought this trouble on us? Today the LORD will bring trouble on you." Then all Israel stoned him. They stoned the rest and burned them with fire.

They piled a large heap of stones over him, which is still there today. Then the LORD turned away from his fierce anger. That is why the place has been called the Valley of Achor, which means Trouble, to this day.
